## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/sheet ``` This also installs `button`, which the sheet uses for its close control and its footer actions. Install `@cadence/checkbox` and `@cadence/field` for the filter composition, and `@cadence/input` for the controlled form. **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority lucide-react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | button | `@components/cadence/button/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) | | sheet | `@components/cadence/sheet/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/sheet.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) [Source files: sheet](https://cadence.dev/r/sheet.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all ten files in the target list, including `button/index.tsx` and every shared `lib/` file. Keep the mirrored `cadence/` tree, relative imports and `"use client"` directives intact. Button is required by Sheet's built-in close control even when your trigger is a native button. The panel and backdrop use CSS transitions, but Button and the provider imports still require `motion`; wrapping your application in `CadenceProvider` is optional. Complete the base theme setup linked above, including Cadence's easing tokens, and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. There is no additional Sheet-specific CSS or asset. Each portalled panel and backdrop resolves its own motion clock, including provider `timeScale`: full fades the backdrop and slides/fades the panel, reduced keeps opacity only, and none removes transitions and hidden entry/exit opacity from the first frame. Without a wrapper, Sheet follows the system motion preference. An explicit nested full scope still respects the system reduced-motion preference. Usage and the top filter specimen additionally need [Checkbox](/components/checkbox) and [Field](/components/field). Controlled form needs Field and [Input](/components/input). Install the items used by the example you copy: ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/checkbox @cadence/field @cadence/input ``` For manual installation, follow those pages' Manual tabs too. The filter adds `checkbox/index.tsx`, `field/index.tsx`, `label/index.tsx` and `separator/index.tsx`; the controlled form adds `field/index.tsx`, `label/index.tsx`, `separator/index.tsx` and `input/index.tsx`. Reuse the shared files already listed here. These compositions add no npm packages beyond Sheet's complete dependency command. The remaining examples need only Sheet, the included Button and, for Explicit motion scopes, the included provider. The built-in close icon comes from the required `lucide-react` dependency. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup. In Next.js App Router, Usage, the top filter specimen and Controlled form need a client module for their state and event handlers. A long list needs one for its initial-focus ref. No request or validation is performed. Use `alert-dialog`. - A hint about a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`. - A flow with its own steps and URL. That is a page, not an overlay. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `Sheet` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI dialog root. | | `SheetTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the sheet. | | `SheetContent` | `side` (`"right" \| "left" \| "top" \| "bottom"`), `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. | | `SheetOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `SheetContent`. | | `SheetPortal` | `container` | Available for a custom portal target. | | `SheetClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the sheet. | | `SheetHeader` / `SheetFooter` | `className` | Padding and stacking only. | | `SheetTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. | | `SheetDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. | ## Motion contract Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `translate` from its own size; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.base` / `duration.fast` | yes | | exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `translate` back off its edge; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · panel `duration.base` / backdrop `duration.fast` | yes | | reduced | opacity only, no translate; at `timeScale={1}`, default duration tokens run at 0.6×: panel 132ms / backdrop 96ms | `exit.fade` | yes | | none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel is in place on the first frame | – | – | The slide is `translate-*-full`, the panel's own width or height, not a fixed distance: a side panel should enter from off its edge at every size, and a distance token would need one value per side. The transition list names `translate` rather than `transform` because Tailwind v4's `translate-*` utilities write the property individually — the same reason the dialogs transition `scale`. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the sheet; focus never reaches the page behind it. | | Escape | Closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger. | | Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. | The panel and backdrop resolve local token clocks from the effective mode and time scale, including full inside a parent none scope. None also removes starting/ending opacity classes, so no hidden starting frame remains. Caller state callback classes/styles still merge last. ## Accessibility - Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling. - `SheetTitle` is required: a sheet without an accessible name is invalid. `SheetDescription` becomes the description, so put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph. - The built-in close control is a button with a screen-reader-only "Close" label; it sits in the top-right corner at every side and never traps the focus ring. - A destructive footer action uses `variant="destructive"` plus a specific verb; the colour is never the only signal. ## Responsive behavior A right or left sheet is `w-3/4` capped at `sm:max-w-sm`; a top or bottom sheet spans the width with an auto height. Long content should scroll inside a wrapper (see "A long list"), so the footer stays reachable and the page behind does not move. ## Performance - One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit. - Animates `opacity` and `translate` only: the panel is `fixed` at its edge, so nothing reflows and the page behind never reads layout. - The close control is a `Button`, so its press feedback obeys the same motion mode as the sheet. ## Notes for AI - Use `sheet` for a task beside the page; use `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate, and `popover` when the content is small and anchored to a control. - Always render `SheetTitle`; put the side effect of closing (reset, discard) in the footer, not in the title. - Name the footer action after its effect ("Apply filters"), not "OK". - If the sheet opens a form, remember P11: the sheet renders invalid state from `aria-invalid` but never validates anything itself.
